$about: DOC-12 round, 2026-08-06: the landing page defect (four places stating 0.8.12 beside one stating 0.8.13) fixed at the page and, more importantly, at the two guards that reported green while it shipped. Run against this project's own repository, which is the target kind 'self' - self-assessment, never counted among the third-party repositories tested. Every quotation below is literal output from a command run in the working tree at the commit this observation lands with. The second observation retires this case's 2026-08-04 row, which was filed against the greenfield fixture because that whole round was: the fixture has no landing page, so the finding was never really about it. The 2026-08-04 file is left exactly as written, the way SHAPE-08 was retired earlier today.

observations.evidence: Reproduced first: `grep -o '[0-9]*\.[0-9]*\.[0-9]*' site/index.html | sort | uniq -c` returned `4 0.8.12` and `1 0.8.13` (plus 15 coordinate triples from SVG path data), against `VERSION` = 0.8.13 - the header pill correct, the maturity disclosure (line 973), the footer (line 983) and two hero-script lines (1010, 1018) a release behind. Both guards were green on that exact tree: `node tools/site-check.mjs` printed `ok    site/index.html: advertises v0.8.13 (matches VERSION)` and exited `site-check: OK - landing + docsite shippable`, and `node standard/scripts/facts-check.mjs` printed `ok    standard-version = 0.8.13 - 5 restatement(s) agree`, because its only declared pattern for this file (`class="tag mono">v`) points at the one occurrence that was right. Fixed: the four strings now read 0.8.13, and site-check compares every version-shaped string on the landing against VERSION rather than asserting one of them appears - `ok    site/index.html: all 5 version string(s) on the page state 0.8.13`. Verified the new check actually fires by putting the footer back to v0.8.12 on the real landing: `FAIL  site/index.html:983: states 0.8.12, and VERSION says 0.8.13 ("...<span>repository-standards · v0.8.12 · MIT<...")`, `site-check: FAIL - 1 problem(s)` - while facts-check on that same tree still printed `ok    standard-version = 0.8.13 - 5 restatement(s) agree`, confirming the gap was site-check's to close. Exactly one problem was reported, not eighteen, because `<svg>` bodies are masked before the scan: the landing's own marks carry 17 version-shaped coordinate triples (6.1.8, 3.3.7, 1.2.1, 0.9.8 and so on), and a check that failed on those would have been switched off within a day. `tools/site-check-test.mjs` is new and holds the behaviour: 6 cases over fixture sites, `site-check-test: OK - 6 cases, a landing carrying a second version cannot pass`, including a fixture whose path data is literally `d="M1.9.9 4.5.6 2.3.9"` next to a correct version, and a stale-footer case asserting the run reports `FAIL - 1 problem(s)` so the mask cannot silently stop working. Mutation-tested rather than assumed: reverting the scan and re-running printed `site-check-test: FAIL - 5 of 6 cases`, and the sixth is the pre-existing advertise criterion, which is meant to survive. The branch's own self-review found a real defect in the first version of the mask - it paired any `<svg` with the next `</svg>`, so a self-closing `<svg class="x"/>` earlier on the page would have blanked out everything up to the following mark, hiding a stale version and reporting the page clean. Reproduced in isolation (`old regex leaves: []` where the hardened one leaves `["0.8.12"]`), fixed by requiring the opening tag to be a real container, and pinned by a sixth case that goes red against the old regex and only that one. No new facts.json patterns: the remaining four occurrences are prose, footer layout and hero copy, and facts-check fails when a declared pattern stops matching, so enumerating them would block the next rewording and still miss whatever is added after - the scan needs no list. Recorded as a caveat rather than hidden: this fixes the landing this repository publishes, and no mechanism yet stops a stale version on an ecosystem sibling's landing that carries its own VERSION.

Retires the 2026-08-04 row for this pair rather than rewriting it. That round filed every promise-inventory finding against this fixture, and its own evidence says the defect was 'reproduced live against the real deployed site' - the fixture is a greenfield Layer-1 tree with no landing page, no VERSION pill and no site-check to run, so this case cannot pass or fail against it. The finding is real and is recorded, fixed, against the repository it actually lives in: the observation above, same file.
